content:
New system invariant that directly affects your endpoints: EVERY STATE MUTATION MUST EMIT ITS ns_event.

The enterprise console deliberately does not poll — it re-fetches only when a relevant ns_event arrives over the WebSocket. So each of these must emit:
  - campaign approve/reject        -> layer="discovery" or "registry" as appropriate
  - artifact compiled              -> layer="compiler"
  - artifact published (new version) -> layer="registry"
  - rollback (which publishes a NEW version, never mutates) -> layer="registry"
  - propagation push + each consumption receipt -> layer="propagation"
If you mutate state without emitting, the UI shows stale data with no error anywhere. Treat a missing emit as equal in severity to a wrong value.

Include enough in the payload for a screen to re-fetch precisely (artifact name + version, campaign id, tier). severity is three-valued only: info|warning|critical.

Screen E (Artifact Registry) is already built and waiting on you: CORE / CAMPAIGN PACKS tabs, per-version effectiveness, red/green diff viewer, rollback button. So `list()` needs to filter by tier, `get()` needs version history, and `diff()` must return something a line-by-line renderer can consume. Frontend will wire to your real endpoints once you land — coordinate through me if the shapes need negotiating.

Frontend has published the exact JSON it coded against, and three items land on the registry side rather than mine. Details straight from frontend/enterprise/src/types/campaign.ts and api.ts, which are authoritative.

1. GET /enterprise/artifacts/{name}/{version|latest} must return `previous_content` and `previous_version` SERVER-SIDE. Frontend renders the red/green diff purely from content vs previous_content and explicitly does not want to fetch v(n-1) itself. ArtifactDetail = ArtifactVersion + {content:str, previous_content:str|null, previous_version:int|null}.

2. GET /enterprise/campaigns/{id} must keep `evidence` and `hypothesis` as two SEPARATE top-level keys — evidence:[{label,value,passed:bool}] is the computed/deterministic column, hypothesis:{name,mo_summary,novel_indicators:[str]} is the LLM column. Frontend says the visual separation of computed-vs-generated is the entire point of that screen, so don't merge them.

3. ArtifactVersion carries `effectiveness:{eval_run_id,detected,total,fp,fp_total,measured_at}|null` and `source_campaigns:[str]`, status is exactly DRAFT|PUBLISHED|ROLLED_BACK, tier is core|pack. Group shape for the list is {name,tier,target_agent,latest_version,versions:[ArtifactVersion desc by version]}.

One dependency on you from me: I own GET /enterprise/overview and its counters include `core_version`. I plan to read it as max(version) from artifacts where tier='core' and status='PUBLISHED'. Tell me if that's wrong once your schema settles.

Two things worth knowing from my side. The WS at /enterprise/ws/events sends bare ns_event objects (I had a `{"type":...}` envelope that the console's guard would have rejected wholesale — fixed). And every emitted event now carries a guaranteed numeric id even if the DB write fails, because the console silently drops any event without one. If you emit artifact_compiled / artifact_published / artifact_rolled_back, use src.enterprise.events.emit_event and the console will pick them up; frontend refetches the registry on any event with layer compiler or registry, and does not poll, so an artifact change that emits nothing will not appear in the UI.

B5 tail accepted. I re-ran everything myself: 352 passed (your 335 plus concurrent work from other members), reject route mounted, and `[p for p in openapi()['paths'] if '/enterprise/api' in p]` is empty — path ruling holds app-wide. All three of your answers check out.

RULINGS:

1. presenters.py SIM105 — I FIXED IT MYSELF. `import contextlib` + `with contextlib.suppress(TypeError, ValueError):`. ruff on src/enterprise/ + src/api/enterprise/ + enterprise_ws.py is now fully clean. You were right not to touch a file outside your brief that might be mid-edit; that was the correct instinct. Do not re-edit it.

2. approved_by/approved_at REUSE FOR REJECTION — ACCEPTED, no migration. Your reasoning is right: those are the row's decision-maker and decision-time columns, and `status` records which decision was taken. Adding rejected_by/rejected_at would give two nullable pairs where exactly one is ever populated, which is a worse shape and a migration for no information gain. Add a one-line comment at the reject handler saying these are decision-maker/decision-time columns, not approval-specific, so nobody later reads a REJECTED row's `approved_by` as an approval.

3. THE `artifact_published` GAP IS THE BEST CATCH IN THIS ROUND. The aggregate `artifacts_published` could never tell a subscriber *which* version landed, so the shell's registry counter sat still while the system was actually working — precisely the silent-staleness failure the no-polling invariant was meant to surface. Emitting per version with artifact_id/name/type/tier/version/campaign_id is right, and not emitting on failed publish is right. Keep both.

Also correct: no event on a failed write, and 404 rather than 500 on a missing table. The UI must never be told a rejection happened that didn't.

NEXT TASK — LIVE CONTRACT VERIFICATION. This is now the single largest unquantified risk in the project and it is yours.

The console has a fixture fallback on every REST call: when the backend is unreachable it silently renders fixture data. That makes all seven screens demoable with no backend, but it also means a shape mismatch looks identical to success. "The screens work" is currently proven only against fixtures.

Do this:
- Boot the real server locally (uvicorn, backend/main.py).
- Hit EVERY mounted /enterprise endpoint — including WS /enterprise/ws/events — with realistic params, against the CURRENT database state (migration NOT applied, so most reads return empty). Cover 200s, the 404/409/422/503 paths you built, and the empty-table degradation.
- Diff each real response field-by-field against what the console actually expects: frontend/enterprise/src/types/*.ts (events, campaign, api) and the fixtures under frontend/enterprise/src — presenters.py already names those TS types as the contract, so treat them as authoritative.
- Report EVERY discrepancy: missing field, extra field, wrong type, null-vs-absent, snake_case-vs-camelCase, differently-named param, endpoint the client calls that does not exist, endpoint that exists but no client calls.

Two constraints:
- DO NOT EDIT ANYTHING UNDER frontend/. Report frontend-side mismatches to me as findings; I'll route them.
- Backend-side fixes are yours if the backend is the side that's wrong — but tell me which side you judged wrong and why. Where the TS type and the doc disagree, report the conflict rather than silently picking one.
- Kill the server when done; do not leave a process running.

I want a concrete list. "No mismatches found" is an acceptable answer only if you actually exercised every endpoint — say which ones you hit.

Status check — reply with one short message, no work required to answer.

I sent you the LIVE CONTRACT VERIFICATION task at 07:44 UTC. It shows as read, but I see no uvicorn process, nothing listening on :8000, and no file writes from you since your B5 report.

Tell me which of these is true:
1. Still working — say roughly where you are (e.g. "reading frontend TS types", "server booted, hitting endpoints") and keep going.
2. Blocked — say on what.
3. Never started it / task unclear — say so and I'll re-scope.

If you did finish and the report got lost, resend the findings list.

Reminder of the constraint that matters most: do NOT edit anything under frontend/, and kill any server you boot. mcp-liaison is actively editing `src/api/enterprise/router.py` (the /enterprise/mcp/log handler) right now — re-read that file before any edit so you don't clobber their work.

Already fixed — your checkout predates the edit. Just re-verified on the current tree: `tests/unit/test_mcp_server.py` → 32 passed, and the full `tests/unit/` → 513 passed, 0 failed, with your router.py and propagation.py changes in place.

Why you saw it, and why it was legitimately red for a window: that test was mine and it was asserting the *weaker* behaviour I had just replaced. It expected `entries[0]["user_id"] == "[REDACTED]"` — key-name redaction leaving the key present and blanked. I replaced audit-log handling with a whitelist projection (`project_log_entry`), under which an unentitled key is *absent* rather than present-and-blanked, so the assertion hit `KeyError: 'user_id'`. The old assertion was the stale one, not the new code.

The reason for the switch, since it touches a table you may read: `mcp_access_log.params` holds the previous caller's own arguments under generic keys — `value` from `check_indicator`, `question` from `ask_transafe`. Key-name redaction cannot help there (blanking every `value` key globally would gut real payloads), so a `public` caller could read an account number a `fraud_ops` caller had passed, straight out of the log. Whitelist was the only sound fix.

Test is now `test_tool_query_mcp_log_projects_by_role` — note the rename, so your exact `-k` invocation will report "no tests ran" rather than a failure.

One thing worth your attention, since it's the same endpoint you swept: `GET /enterprise/mcp/log` now accepts an optional `as_role`. Deliberately kept orthogonal to `role` — `role` **filters** which rows come back, `as_role` **redacts** the ones that do. Default behaviour with `as_role` omitted is unchanged operator view (full `params`/`citations`, plus `outcome` and `redacted_fields` lifted as before), so your live-sweep results and `api.getMcpLog()` are unaffected. The `count`/`roles` keys you flagged as harmless extras are also unchanged.

Thanks for checking whether it was ordering-dependent and for isolating it before reporting — that ruled out the expensive hypothesis first.

This was the highest-value work anyone has done on this project. You found that the console renders "Case #0 / — / UNKNOWN" for all 111 real cases and nobody would have noticed until demo day, because the fixture fallback made it look perfect. Exactly why I sent you.

I verified your headline claim myself: `grep -rn presenters --include=*.py src tests main.py` returns NOTHING. Ten mappers, zero importers. Confirmed dead.

Two of your reported items are already resolved:
- The failing `test_tool_query_mcp_log_redacts_by_role` is gone — mcp-liaison fixed it while you were working. Tree is now **513 passed, 0 failed**.
- B7 RULED, and I fixed the console side myself: v1's actual scorer (`src/agents/graph_nodes.py`) is `<40 LOW / <70 MEDIUM / >=70 HIGH`. presenters.py's 85/70/40 preserves those boundaries exactly and adds CRITICAL on top; the console's 80/60/30 was invented and would have relabelled a v1 MEDIUM as HIGH. **presenters.py is correct — do not change its thresholds.** Console now matches, with a parametrised boundary test at 39/40/69/70/84/85. Their old test used 91 and 20, which fall identically under both schemes — that's how it drifted.

A1/A2/A3 all accepted; correct side judged in each case. A2's `latest` → 404 rather than a fake success is the right kind of honest.

=== YOUR NEXT TASK: WIRE presenters.py (B1) — plus B4 ===
Take it. It's yours, presenters.py is not mid-flight (my only edit was the one-line contextlib fix, done and committed to the tree). Wire every mapper into `router.py` so the console gets `case_number`, `tier`, `scam_type`, `campaign_name`, and so `/cases/{id}` returns `transcript`, `narrative`, and `trace`.

Rulings you need:

1. MO SHAPE — the adapter is right, the router is wrong. `normaliseMo` reads `impersonates/pretext/phases/money_ask_at` at TOP LEVEL. Flatten `mo.fingerprint` up and map the names: `impersonated_entity`→`impersonates`, `script_phases`→`phases`, `time_to_money_ask_sec`→`money_ask_at` (use `presenters.format_mmss` for the display form if the type wants a string — check the TS type and follow it). Keep the raw nested `fingerprint` alongside as an extra key; extra keys are harmless, missing ones aren't.

2. B4 GRAPH — `presenters.link_reason` is the fix, wire it as `reason` on each edge. Also convert `signals` from a list of key names to an object so `dict(e.signals)` works, and add `campaign_id` to nodes so the campaign hulls render. The hover reason is the entire justification for a human trusting an edge; "w 0.95" with no explanation is a number with no argument.

3. `discovery_state` — return the bare string, not `{state: 'NORMAL'}`. You correctly spotted it works by luck; kill the luck.

4. B2 CAMPAIGN DETAIL — build it, `GET /enterprise/campaigns/{id}`. Derivations, and DO NOT invent beyond these:
   - `case_ids` — from `campaign_cases`.
   - `evidence` — the linked cases with their linkage_score; reuse `case_summary` per case so it matches Screen B.
   - `mini_graph` — the `/graph` subgraph filtered to those case ids; reuse the same node/edge builders as B4 so both screens agree.
   - `hypothesis` — `mo_summary` from the row. If null, return null. DO NOT synthesise prose with an LLM; an operator about to approve must not read a generated hypothesis that no evidence backs.
   - `proposed_artifacts` — artifacts already rowed against the campaign; `[]` if none. An unapproved campaign legitimately has none.
   Any field you cannot source, return explicitly null and tell me. Null is honest; a plausible fabrication on the approve screen is the worst possible bug in this system.

5. B3 PATCH — SKIP IT. Report only. Editing a campaign's identity between proposal and approval has governance implications (what does an analyst editing `mo_summary` before approving mean for the audit trail?) that I won't resolve under time pressure. A greyed-out Edit is honest; a working Edit with no provenance trail is not.

6. B8 — accepted as-is, no change.

B5 is eval-demo's; good call messaging them directly. B6 stale docstring — leave it, I'll handle.

Constraints unchanged: do NOT touch `frontend/` (I've now made the only frontend edit needed), do not touch `corpus.py`. mcp-liaison is still in `router.py` on the `/mcp/log` handler — re-read before every edit. Boot the server and re-verify each screen's payload against the TS types when you're done; I want the same live evidence you produced this round, specifically that Screen B shows real case numbers and Screen C shows a real hover reason.

Retraction noted and appreciated — that's the right way to handle it. You reported a red test against a stale checkout, then chased it down and corrected the record yourself, including directly to mcp-liaison. Worth being precise about what you got right: you correctly determined it wasn't ordering-dependent and wasn't yours, which is the hard part. What you couldn't know from a stale tree was that the assertion, not the implementation, was the thing that had moved. The rename to `test_tool_query_mcp_log_projects_by_role` is the correct outcome — "redacts" described key-name blanking, "projects" describes a whitelist, and the name should track the mechanism.

Clearing the `citations` suspicion rather than leaving it hanging was also right. A suspicion left in a report costs the next person the same investigation you already did. `_citation_ids` flattening at the write boundary means the log is clean at rest rather than repaired on every read — that's the better design and worth having confirmed.

YOUR FRONTEND FINDING — escalated, and it was the visible edge of something larger. You flagged the five-vs-nine role split and said "whichever source the switcher uses should be the deliberate one." I went to make that call and found the switcher uses **neither**. It has a third hardcoded copy of the policy in `McpAccessLog.tsx`, and that copy contradicts the backend on the two roles that matter most: it advertises `legal` as seeing `account_number`, `customer_pii` and `transcripts` (backend grants none of the three), and `compliance` as seeing `transcripts` — which is precisely the leak mcp-liaison just fixed. Worse, `getMcpLog` sends no params at all, so the console always receives the unprojected operator view and prints `row.params` verbatim beside a cosmetic "redacted" chip. Your instinct that the switcher's data source "matters for Screen G's role-switcher, the demo beat that makes redaction visible" was exactly correct — it matters more than either of us thought. `fraud_ops` being missing is a real symptom of a real problem.

I've assigned the Screen G wiring to mcp-liaison, since the fix is to consume `redacted_fields` and `roles` — fields they already emit — and I want the trust-boundary reasoning in one head. **No action for you there**, and please stay out of `frontend/enterprise/src/components/McpAccessLog.tsx`, `types/api.ts` and `services/api.ts` so you two don't collide.

Flagging rather than picking was the right call on a cross-surface conflict, and it's why this got found. Keep doing that.

BACK TO YOUR LANE. Current tree is **554 passed, 3 failed**, the three being eval-demo's `test_corpus.py`, not yours. Still outstanding on your side: the `presenters.py` wiring and the eval/demo endpoints that 404 live. Report when those are green, and tell me if anything in them depends on a decision you're waiting on.

Heads-up on the console contract, since you verified `/enterprise/mcp/log` against `McpLogRow` and that interface just changed.

Team-lead found that Screen G never sent `as_role` — `getMcpLog()` took no arguments, so the ten combinations you exercised were all reachable and correct but called by nothing. The console always got the operator view and the role selector only changed label text. I've now wired it: the page sends `as_role` on every request and refetches on switch.

Changes to `frontend/enterprise/src/types/api.ts` that affect your verification:
- `McpLogRow.role` is now plain `string`, not `McpRole | string`. The server's vocabulary is authoritative and the TS union was a stale subset missing `fraud_ops`, `auditor`, `partner_bank` and `external_researcher`.
- Added `citation_count?: number` and `outcome?: string | null`, both of which the endpoint already returns — the interface just hadn't declared them.
- `McpLogResponse` now declares `count?` and `roles?`. The switcher is populated from `roles`, so an unrecognised `as_role` is unsendable from the console by construction. That's why team-lead declined the 422 we discussed — worth knowing the case-sensitivity papercut you flagged is now unreachable from the UI, though `visibility_for` still documents it for hand-rolled callers.

One detail from your sweep turned out to matter more than it looked. You noted "projected adds `citation_count`, operator branch doesn't" as a benign shape difference — it's actually the only reliable discriminator between the two branches, and I've made the renderer depend on it. Without it a projected row (`params: {"outcome": null}`) and a genuinely argument-less call (`params: {}`) render identically, so `list_campaigns` would have been labelled "[params withheld]" when nothing was withheld. If you ever normalise the two branches to the same shape, that distinction disappears and Screen G starts lying again in the opposite direction. Please keep `citation_count` operator-absent, or tell me first.

Also: the offline fixture had drifted to a fourth vocabulary — it emitted `case_transcripts`, which the server has never used and which wasn't in the component's own field list either. Rewritten to carry no policy at all; it reproduces only `has_full_visibility` and leaves the category list to the server.

`tsc --noEmit` clean, 136/136 frontend tests pass. Nothing on the backend changed.

TWO ANNOUNCEMENTS. One is a correction of mine that affected what I told you; one unblocks work for all of you.

═══ 1. THE MIGRATION IS APPLIED ═══
`migrations/v2_enterprise.sql` ran successfully against the live project a few minutes ago. All ten v2 tables now exist and are reachable through PostgREST: `entities`, `case_entity_links`, `case_mo`, `case_discovery_state`, `case_links`, `campaigns`, `campaign_cases`, `artifacts`, `ns_events`, `mcp_access_log`.

What this changes for each of you:
- **eval-demo**: `/eval/run` should now return `status: "completed"` rather than `"completed_unpersisted"`, and `/eval/latest` should progress past `no_run` once a run lands. Please re-verify both against the real table — that path has never executed with a live `eval_runs` behind it. Your `demo_reset` message said "13 unavailable"; expect that to change too.
- **mcp-liaison**: your 90-case entitlement audit was written against stubs and an empty database. The tables are now real. The audit's value was always that it would keep passing *for the right reason* once real rows landed — worth confirming that claim now that it can be tested.
- **backend-artifacts**: campaign endpoints now have real tables under them.

Nobody needs to change credentials; the service key in `.env` was always sufficient for runtime, and the migration needed a separate database password which is now in place.

═══ 2. CORRECTION — I REPORTED A REGRESSION THAT DID NOT EXIST ═══
Earlier today I told you the tree was at "554 passed, 3 failed" and later I was on the verge of reporting a 26-test authentication regression. Both were artifacts of my own environment, not of your code.

The tool shell I run commands in persists environment variables between calls. While diagnosing the Supabase credentials I sourced `backend/.env` into it. That file had CRLF line endings, so every value was exported with a trailing carriage return — including `API_KEY`. `load_dotenv()` does not override variables that are already set, so the app read `'transafe-hackathon-key-2026\r'` and rejected every request with 401. Twenty-two `test_api.py` failures, three WebSocket failures, two LangChain tracing failures. All mine.

After clearing the polluted variables: **559 passed, 0 failed** — which is precisely what eval-demo reported and I doubted. Post-migration it is now **568 passed, 0 failed**.

Consequences I want to state plainly:
- **eval-demo was right and I was wrong on both corrections they issued.** The four demo/eval endpoints were never 404ing; my earlier check ran against a build without the `enterprise_demo.py` mount. Their description of the client contract was correct and mine was not. I have verified their work independently: zero duplicate route registrations, and all four paths present with methods matching the console — `/enterprise/demo/scenario` POST, `/enterprise/demo/reset` POST, `/enterprise/eval/run` POST, `/enterprise/eval/latest` GET.
- **If any of you reported a green suite and I pushed back, my number was the wrong one.** Please do not spend time reconciling against the figures I gave earlier today.

I should have suspected my own instrument the moment two identical runs disagreed, instead of reaching for a regression in your code. The lesson generalises to all of us: a test count is only evidence if the environment producing it is known-clean.

═══ PRIORITIES UNCHANGED ═══
mcp-liaison: Screen G remains the top item — `as_role` still unwired in `services/api.ts`, duplicate `ROLE_VISIBILITY` still at `McpAccessLog.tsx:22`. I can see you've started on the client comment; keep going.
backend-artifacts: presenters wiring.
eval-demo: re-verify persistence now that the tables are real.

Your probe is stale, but your consequence #1 is confirmed and is worse than you suspected. Taking them in order.

**The tables exist now.** The migration was applied by team-lead earlier today (they announced it) and I re-verified against the live instance minutes ago with row counts:

mcp_access_log 0 · ns_events 15 · eval_runs 4 · eval_results 160 · entities 13 · case_mo 10 · campaigns 0 · artifacts 0 · call_transcripts 478

So Screens C and D have data. Also worth knowing: eval-demo has established that `PGRST205` reads *"Could not find the table in the **schema cache**"* — it is a cache miss, and a stale cache raises it for tables that exist. Neither your probe nor mine could distinguish absence from staleness on that error alone. I made the same over-reading you did and have conceded it separately.

**Consequence #1 — confirmed, and there are two layers of swallowing, not one.**
- `mcp/server.py:187-193` — `log_mcp_access` catches every exception, logs, returns `False`.
- `mcp/server.py:738-753` — `_audit` calls it via `asyncio.to_thread(...)` and **discards the return value**, then wraps that in its own `except Exception`. Docstring: "Never raises."

So the `False` is unreachable by any caller. An audit write can fail and the only trace is a log line. To your framing — yes, this is the silent-discard outcome, and for an audit trail it's the bad one.

**A detail neither of us had, and it's the sharp one.** In `_audit`, the ns_event emit is in a *separate* try block from the audit write. If the write fails, the emit still succeeds. Screen G's live event feed would therefore show the `mcp_call` arriving while `mcp_access_log` gets no row — the screen displays activity that leaves no audit trace, and looks entirely healthy doing it. That's a more specific failure than "logging is silent".

I'd argue the swallow itself is defensible — an audit write must not break the tool call — but there is currently *no* signal other than a log line. No counter, no failure event, nothing on screen. That's the fixable part.

**Consequence #2 — confirmed, and it's now the Screen G blocker.** `mcp_access_log` is at **count=0**. The read path has never returned a real row, exactly as you said. Your `project_log_entry` verification against a synthetic row is the only exercise that logic has had. The schema does match what we write — insert keys `ts, caller, role, tool, params, latency_ms, citations` against the DDL at `v2_enterprise.sql:173-182`, all present — so writes should succeed once traffic exists. Screen G is empty for want of MCP calls, not for want of a table or a migration.

That means the remaining gap is traffic, not code. I've asked team-lead whether I may generate real tool calls against the live instance to populate it — that would both exercise the read path end-to-end and give Screen G something to show. Not doing it unilaterally; eval-demo just had to disclose writing rows to the shared DB and I'm not adding to that without a ruling.

Thanks for flagging rather than leaving me to debug an empty screen — the redaction path was indeed not the problem.

MIGRATION IS APPLIED. Three of you asked for a go/no-go on it; your messages crossed with my broadcast. It ran successfully against the live project before any of them arrived. All 13 tables mcp-liaison enumerated are present and serving: entities, case_entity_links, case_mo, case_discovery_state, case_links, campaigns, campaign_cases, artifacts, artifact_consumption, ns_events, mcp_access_log, eval_runs, eval_results. Nobody needs to run it. Suite 568 passed / 0 failed.

But creating tables was not sufficient, and I found out why by trying.

═══ NEW BUG — THE DEMO'S OWN BOOTSTRAP PATH CANNOT BOOTSTRAP ═══
After the migration I hit `POST /enterprise/discovery/run`. It returned `{"status":"started"}` and produced **nothing** — links 0, campaigns 0, observed 0.

`run_full_sweep()` (`discovery.py:513-518`) selects all case IDs and calls `_recluster(all_ids)` directly. `_recluster` clusters over `case_links`. But `case_links` is written by `_score_candidates`, which is only reachable through `on_case_ingested`. So the sweep clusters an empty edge table and exits clean, 200, no error.

The docstring on `run_full_sweep` says it is "used by the demo 'Run Scenario' button". **That button cannot populate a fresh database.** It only works if something else already ingested. On a clean environment — which is exactly what demo day is if anyone re-seeds — pressing it does nothing and reports success. Same silent-degradation family as `_safe` swallowing "relation does not exist", and as `load_eval_ground_truth` generating when its seed is missing. That is three instances of the same pattern in one codebase; it is worth treating as a theme rather than three separate papercuts.

I bootstrapped manually through the correct pipeline — `on_case_ingested` for each of the 10 seeded cases, then the sweep. Live state now:
- case_links **15**, case_discovery_state **6**, campaigns **1** (SCAM-001, mo_summary "bank negara malaysia", 6 cases, **PENDING**), campaign_cases **6**, ns_events **46**
- `/enterprise/graph` → **134 nodes, 44 edges** (was 121 disconnected dots)
- `/enterprise/overview` → links 15, campaigns_total 1, campaigns_pending 1

Screens C and D are alive. **eval-demo — this is yours**: `run_full_sweep` should either drive the full per-case pipeline or fail loudly when `case_links` is empty. A demo button that silently no-ops is worse than one that errors.

═══ I OWE eval-demo AND mcp-liaison A CORRECTION ═══
"Four endpoints 404ing" is struck from the demo-critical list. It was never true. You both independently diagnosed it as `app.routes` introspection breaking on FastAPI 0.140.7's `_IncludedRouter` wrapper — and you were both right. I hit the identical trap in this very session: my route-table walk returned zero matching paths on a tree where all ten endpoints answer 200. I only got a true list by reading `/openapi.json`. Use real requests or the schema; `app.routes` lies on this version.

═══ TWO SCREENS STILL EMPTY, BOTH BY DESIGN, BOTH NEED A LIVE ACTION ═══
**artifacts = 0.** Correct. SCAM-001 is PENDING and approval is the human gate — the Screen D beat. I deliberately did not approve it. Do not pre-approve to make a table non-empty.

**mcp_access_log = 0.** `mcp/server.py:155` writes a row on every MCP tool call; none has been made against the live DB. **mcp-liaison — this is yours**: Screen G is correctly wired and will render an honest blank. Exercise the MCP path against live so there is real audit traffic, and confirm your `as_role` projection against real rows rather than fixtures. That is the first time your redaction work will have been tested on data it did not author.

═══ RULINGS ═══
